subject.title: [Telegram] 机器人头像更改后无法同步到 Telegram 客户端

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in Telegram plugin path that can change a bot's public profile photo from the configured agent avatar, or should bot profile photos remain a manual BotFather/account-administration task?
rationale: This changes a bot's public identity through stored Telegram credentials and likely adds new action/config/API surface, so automation should not choose the security boundary or UX model without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve explicit opt-in action
options.body: Add a Telegram plugin-owned `set-bot-avatar` or similarly named action using the current bot self-profile API, default off, with media validation, docs, tests, and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Keep manual BotFather flow
options.body: Close or document the request as account administration if maintainers do not want OpenClaw mutating Telegram bot profile identity.

options.title: Explore automatic sync later
options.body: Defer bidirectional avatar watching until maintainers define how Web UI overrides, config avatars, token ownership, audit, and failure recovery should work.

recommendation.title: Approve explicit opt-in action
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram plugin-owned `set-bot-avatar` or similarly named action using the current bot self-profile API, default off, with media validation, docs, tests, and live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter appears as the heaviest Telegram action/send history contributor and is the likely owner for deciding a new security-sensitive identity mutation surface.
